scenarios.name: Incoming service request
scenarios.narrative: A submitted request starts the process. The coordinator records it, assigns a specialist, and the specialist completes the work. Completion ends the process.

scenarios.name: Expense approval
scenarios.narrative: An employee submits an expense. A manager checks whether it meets policy. If it does, Accounts Payable reimburses it and closes it as paid. Otherwise the manager declines it and closes it as declined.

scenarios.name: Support case triage
scenarios.narrative: Support receives a case, then classifies it as billing, technical, account access, or unclassified. Each category goes to its named specialist; unclassified goes to a triage lead. Every route returns a resolution to support, which notifies the customer and closes the case.

scenarios.name: Purchase approval with escalation
scenarios.narrative: A purchase request is checked for completeness. Missing details return to the requester and are checked again. A complete request under the threshold goes directly to ordering. A request at or over the threshold goes to a director. The director approves it for ordering or declines it, ending the request. After ordering, delivery is checked. A mismatch is resolved with the supplier and delivery is checked again; accepted delivery ends the process.

scenarios.name: Employee onboarding
scenarios.narrative: After a signed offer arrives, HR launches identity checks, IT account setup, and facilities desk preparation at the same time. Identity checks may require a corrected document and recheck. HR waits until identity checks, IT accounts, and desk preparation are all complete before sending the welcome pack and marking onboarding ready.

scenarios.name: Report availability check
scenarios.narrative: An analyst starts a scheduled report check. The analyst checks whether the report is available. If not, the analyst repeats the same availability check; if it is, the analyst downloads it and ends the check.

scenarios.name: Monthly account reconciliation
scenarios.narrative: Month end starts reconciliation. An analyst retrieves transactions from the ledger database and downloads the bank statement. The analyst compares the records. If totals differ, the analyst records the discrepancy in the exceptions register, obtains a correction, and compares again. If totals agree, the reviewer signs the reconciliation report, the analyst archives it in the records repository, and the close ends.

scenarios.name: Supplier onboarding with waiting and delegation
scenarios.narrative: A buyer requests a new supplier. Procurement runs its separate supplier due-diligence procedure, whose internal steps are outside this interview. Procurement then waits for the signed supplier contract. Once it arrives, procurement checks the signature. An invalid signature is returned for correction and procurement waits again. A valid contract is recorded in the supplier master, then the supplier is activated and onboarding ends.

scenarios.name: Customer response and escalation
scenarios.narrative: After support requests information, support waits up to three business days for a response. A response within that period goes to assessment. If the deadline passes, support sends one reminder and waits another two days. A response then goes to assessment. No response after that second deadline closes the case as inactive. Assessment resolves the case and closes it as resolved.

scenarios.name: Partially described reporting work
scenarios.narrative: I prepare a weekly status report and send it to my manager. Separately I maintain a risks register, but I have not explained when that happens or whether it connects to reporting. I do not know the overall trigger or what happens after the manager receives the report.

scenarios.name: Parallel onboarding with alternative verification outcomes
scenarios.narrative: A signed offer starts onboarding. HR launches identity verification, IT account setup, and desk preparation in parallel. HR checks the identity documents. Accepted documents complete identity verification immediately. Otherwise the employee corrects the documents, HR rechecks them, and an accepted recheck completes identity verification; a failed recheck returns for another correction. Initial acceptance or accepted recheck are alternatives: either one completes the same identity-verification branch. HR waits for that identity branch, IT accounts, and the desk to all be ready before sending the welcome pack and ending onboarding.

scenarios.name: Cross-border evidence review and international handoff
scenarios.narrative: A specialist receives an amended cross-border instruction with multilingual identifiers. They validate every account identifier against the approved documentation. If the beneficiary identifier, currency, settlement reference, and supporting approval all match, they send the complete package to the regional operations and quality-assurance team. If any item is incomplete or mismatched, they return it to the originating relationship team for documented correction and recheck. The regional team records the final review in the cross-border exception-management repository and finishes the review.

scenarios.name: Eighty-step sequential control walkthrough
scenarios.narrative: A synthetic stress test reports eighty sequential processing checkpoints, handed from one team to the next after every tenth checkpoint. This fixture tests the renderer's documented 80-step capacity; it does not claim any real process or infer extra branches.
